scenes.headline: How SigLIP 2 learns to match photos and captions
scenes.sub: A pairwise sigmoid loss, plus training heads that never ship.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Lovage! SigLIP 2 turns photos and captions into vectors you can compare. Here's how it learns.

scenes.label: The idea
scenes.text: Ask one yes-or-no question for every image-caption pair, so no pair waits on the rest of the batch. Then add training heads that never ship.
scenes.say: The idea: one yes or no question per image and caption pair, so no pair waits on the batch. Plus extra training heads, dropped at release.

scenes.title: Softmax couples a row. Sigmoid does not.

steps.label: matching pairs
steps.say: Photos down the side, captions across. The matches sit on the diagonal, and every other cell is a free negative.

steps.label: softmax: one row
steps.say: CLIP's softmax makes each photo pick its caption from the whole row. Move one cell, and the gradients across that row move with it.

steps.label: sigmoid: block by block
steps.say: SigLIP asks each cell on its own. So every device works block by block, and nobody gathers the full batch.

parts.note: image vector · caption vector, both unit length
parts.say: The cosine between the image vector and the caption vector,
plus a learned bias that starts every pair leaning towards no, since almost every pair is a mismatch.

steps.say: A photo and a caption each get their own encoder, and the pooled vectors meet in the sigmoid loss.
SigLIP 2 adds a decoder on the patch features that writes captions and finds boxes for phrases.
Late in training, an EMA teacher makes it match whole-image features from crops and masked patches. Neither head ships.

scenes.title: Sorting 7,349 pet photos
scenes.say: FluidInference's Core ML port sorts seven thousand three hundred forty nine pet photos in thirty six seconds, against a hundred and two for full precision PyTorch on the Mac's GPU. Same accuracy.

scenes.text: The extra objectives are scaffolding for training. What ships is two encoders, one dot product, one sigmoid.
scenes.mark: two encoders, one dot product, one sigmoid

recap: One sigmoid question per image-caption pair
Decoder and EMA teacher train it, then vanish
Core ML port: half the bytes, same accuracy
scenes.say: To recap: one sigmoid question per pair, training heads that vanish, and a faithful half size port.
